reviews.text: 2 saat boyunca kardinallerin koridorlarda dedikodu yapmasını izlediğimiz, aşırı abartılmış sıkıcı bir film. Vatikan'ın kapalı kapılar ardındaki entrikalarını çok derin bir şeymiş gibi pazarlamışlar ama temelde insanı esneten sıkıcı bir hikaye olmaktan öteye geçemiyor finalde de ucuz bir sürpriz sonla bağlanıp bitiyor. Özetle beğenmedim. O yıl Anora'nın Oscar'ı hak edip etmediği tartışılır ama Conclave'den iyi olduğu kesin.

C'était acceptable. Sujet original et plein de mystère qui tient en haleine, une réalisation sobre et carrée, un cast solide avec un Fiennes qui nous sort sa plus belle gueule de Droopy pendant 2h. Mais ça souffre quand même de quelques soucis d'écriture (le perso de Aldo en particulier, mais pas que) et d'une dernière demi heure qui vire à la blague hollywoodienne neuneuïsante qui vient briser toute trace de crédibilité dans l'histoire racontée. C'est mignon mais c'est con.

Num geral, é um filme bom, muito bem produzido, com ótimos personagens, atores, figurinos, críticas muito bem trabalhadas e construtivas, além de cenas de tensão muito boas. Porém, esse final do filme estraga TUDO. Colocar a revelação de que um cardeal hermafrodita foi escolhido pelo Conclave para ser o papa só para forçar mensagens políticamente ideológicas foi absurdo de ruim, e um enorme desrespeito com a igreja Católica de graça. Até eu que nem sou católico me ofendi com essa blasfêmia. Estragou o filme, então um honesto 5/10. (Além do que eu quase ia esquecendo de falar: esse papa foi eleito de forma apressada e sem nexo por causa de um discurso contra o cardeal Tedesco, simplesmente por reclamar dele estar utilizando a "ira" contra os terroristas Islâmicos que tinham atacado a igreja horas antes. Mesmo com as críticas sendo boas e necessárias, eu acho um exagero tratar o Tedesco como vilão do início ao fim do filme só por ele ser conservador).

conclave isn’t bad at all, but this is genuinely one of the more disappointing movies i’ve watched. i went into it with pretty high expectations because the whole setup sounded SO interesting, and the movie definitely has the ingredients for something incredible. the Vatican setting, the secretive atmosphere, the politics, everyone hiding something… i was ready to be completely hooked. Ralph Fiennes was really good though, and i liked watching Cardinal Lawrence try to keep everything under control while slowly realizing that basically everyone around him has their own agenda. the whole process of the conclave was probably my favourite part because there’s this constant feeling that one little reveal could completely change everything. but the actual mystery just didn’t hit me as hard as i wanted it to. there were some twists that were interesting, but by the end i was more like “oh… okay” than completely shocked. i think that’s what disappointed me most because the movie spends so much time building up this huge sense of intrigue that i expected the payoff to absolutely destroy me. it’s still really well-made, the performances are strong and the atmosphere is great, but i just wanted MORE from it. maybe if i hadn’t gone in with such high expectations i’d feel differently.

The drama…  This was pretty impressive. I liked how it committed to the lockdown of these people and so so little of the outside world. Definitely very watchable. I enjoyed main character and their crisis of faith. But I can’t say I found this great, maybe in part because of a level of unbelievability in some of these ‘great men’ and how they react to pivotal moments in their own life. In particular the final vote where it felt a bit like believability was yeeted out the blown window to make room for The Point to be made and not missed. Still. I liked the point well enough. And the twist of the point was kinda interesting, if rather unexplored by necessity of the locked in constraint. Still, interesting and wasn’t bored. “I don’t want your vote.” “Nevertheless you have it.”

• This landed a bit below my expectations but it was still a fine, high-brow drama with tense moments, good music, and well-built characters. • Fiennes is astonishingly good in this movie, to the point that he outshines the likes of Lithgow and Tucci (but not Rossellini) in their scenes together • One thing I liked was that through all this nasty politics the reverence for the previous Pope (at least among his supporters) is clear. It’s as if the Pope can do no wrong, if anything was his doing, it becomes “okay”, and yet all the suitors for the next papacy are clearly prone to questionable decisions. • Cardinal Lawrence is perhaps a bit too pure, he is the protagonist but he doesn’t really show any impure notions the whole movie

Le Pape est mort. Au Vatican, un conclave se forme pour désigner qui succédera au Saint-Père. Structurellement composé de suspense, Conclave, nous plonge dans les coulisses de « l’Entreprise » la plus vieille au monde. La mise en scène d’Edward Berger installe une ambiance feutrée aux airs de Polar huit clos, porté par un casting international cohérent avec le propos, Ici ce n’est pas tant l’élection qui importe mais ce besoin de justesse que cherche sans fin le Cardinal Lawrence, joué par Ralph Fiennes. Sujet objectivement sensible, le film ne manquera pas d’évoquer les dernières casseroles que tirent l’Eglise, sans en faire le sous thème de son film. J’en retiens 20 minutes de trop, ralentissant un rythme déjà peu dynamique compte tenu de l’Arene (le Vatican) et de ses composants (les Cardinaux). Pas la plus grande révélation mais un sujet intéressant avec un vrai plus sur la mise en scène et la musique
